recipe.title: Laura's Cookies
recipe.subtitle: Copycat · 2.5-hour version
recipe.description: Soft sour-cream sugar cookies with almond icing, streamlined for a same-day baking and frosting session.

items: 1 cup (226 g / 2 sticks) unsalted real butter, softened

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Cream butter and sugar for 2–3 minutes. Beat in eggs one at a time, then vanilla and sour cream. Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt separately; gradually mix dry ingredients into wet, stopping as soon as combined.

steps.title: Freezer-chill
steps.text: Cover the bowl tightly and freeze for 45 minutes. Check at 25 minutes: the dough should become very cold and firm enough to roll, not frozen solid.

steps.title: Preheat and prepare
steps.text: Near the end of the chill, heat oven to 350°F and line baking sheets with parchment.

steps.title: Roll and cut
steps.text: Lightly flour the counter and roll dough ⅜ inch thick. Cut shapes and transfer to parchment-lined trays.

steps.title: Freeze the trays
steps.text: Skip the long refrigerator chill. Freeze each finished tray for 7–10 minutes to quickly firm the butter.

steps.title: Bake pale
steps.text: Bake at 350°F for 9–11 minutes. Start checking at 9 minutes. Keep the cookies pale rather than waiting for golden edges.

steps.title: Cool and frost
steps.text: Leave cookies on the sheet 3 minutes, then transfer to a rack. Whisk powdered sugar, milk, almond extract, and salt until thick and smooth. Once cookies are fully cool, frost and let icing set 20–30 minutes.

recipe.note: Do not skip the initial 45-minute freezer chill. That first chill, plus a 7–10 minute tray freeze, makes thick sour-cream dough workable within the 2½-hour plan.

recipe.title: White Cheddar
recipe.subtitle: Apple chicken chili
recipe.description: A thick, savory white chicken chili with apple cider flavor, warm spice, green chile, and plenty of white cheddar, without apple pieces.

items: 1½ lb boneless, skinless chicken breast, chopped bite-size
5 cups water + chicken bouillon for 5 cups broth
1 cup apple juice or apple cider
1 can Great Northern beans, drained and rinsed
1 can black beans, drained and rinsed
2 cans garbanzo beans, drained and rinsed
2 cups sharp white cheddar, freshly shredded
½ cup Monterey Jack, Colby Jack, or another mild melting cheese
1 tsp each smoked paprika, dried oregano, and garlic powder
¼ tsp cinnamon + tiny pinch nutmeg
1 tbsp brown sugar or maple syrup, optional
Salt, only at the end if needed

steps.title: Sauté onion and garlic
steps.text: Melt butter in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Cook onion about 5 minutes until softened, then add garlic for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Season the chicken
steps.text: Add chopped chicken, cumin, chili powder, smoked paprika, oregano, garlic powder, onion powder, pepper, cinnamon, nutmeg, and cayenne if using. Cook 5–6 minutes, stirring occasionally.

steps.title: Add broth and apple flavor
steps.text: Pour in water and bouillon, then add apple juice or cider. Cider has the deeper apple flavor. Stir in diced green chiles.

steps.title: Add mashed and whole beans
steps.text: Drain and rinse all four cans of beans. Mash about 1½ cups of the Great Northern and garbanzo beans thoroughly, then add the mashed beans plus all remaining whole beans to the pot.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Bring to a gentle boil, reduce to medium-low, and simmer uncovered 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add up to ½ cup more water if it becomes thicker than you like.

steps.title: Balance the flavor
steps.text: After about 20 minutes, taste. Add brown sugar or maple syrup if you want a subtle sweet apple-cheddar balance.

steps.title: Add milk and cheese
steps.text: Turn heat to low. Slowly stir in milk and warm 2–3 minutes without hard-boiling. Add cheeses a handful at a time, stirring until smooth.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Turn off heat and let chili rest 10 minutes. It will thicken noticeably before serving.

recipe.note: The goal is savory chicken, white cheddar, and mild green chile with a noticeable but never dessert-like apple sweetness. Do not skip the apple juice or cider when leaving out apple chunks.

recipe.title: Copycat Skyline
recipe.subtitle: Cincinnati chili
recipe.description: A finely textured, warmly spiced Cincinnati-style meat sauce for spaghetti, coneys, or a classic three-way.

items: 1 tsp each cinnamon, garlic powder, and cumin
¼ tsp each allspice, ground cloves, and red pepper flakes
¾ tsp salt + ½ tsp sugar
Diced onion, kidney beans, oyster crackers, and hot sauce

steps.title: Build the base
steps.text: Add water, tomato paste, and baking chocolate to a Dutch oven or large pot. Heat over medium, whisking for about 3 minutes until the tomato paste is smooth and the chocolate melts.

steps.title: Add the seasonings
steps.text: Stir in chili powder, cinnamon, garlic powder, cumin, allspice, cloves, red pepper flakes, black pepper, salt, sugar, and apple cider vinegar.

steps.title: Crumble the beef
steps.text: Add the raw ground beef and break it into very fine pieces with clean fingers, a potato masher, whisk, or fork. Fine pieces are essential for the signature texture.

steps.title: Bring to a boil
steps.text: Raise the heat to bring the chili to a boil, stirring so the meat stays evenly broken up.

steps.title: Low-boil until thick
steps.text: Lower heat to medium-low and cook uncovered at a gentle boil for 1–1½ hours. Stir occasionally until it thickens into a rich meat sauce.

steps.title: Serve a Cincinnati way
steps.text: For a three-way, spoon chili over thin spaghetti and pile on cheddar. Add onions or beans for a four-way, both for a five-way, or serve over hot dogs for coneys.

recipe.note: Starting raw beef in the liquid is intentional. It produces the smooth, fine-grained texture that makes Cincinnati chili different from a regular bowl of chili.

recipe.title: The Best
recipe.subtitle: Classic chili
recipe.description: A quick, traditional beef-and-bean chili with a full homemade spice blend and just enough heat.

items: 1 can (15 oz) petite diced tomatoes, with juice
1 can (16 oz) red kidney beans, drained and rinsed
¼ tsp ground cayenne pepper, optional

steps.title: Cook the onion
steps.text: Heat olive oil in a large soup pot over medium-high heat for 2 minutes. Add diced onion and cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.text: Add ground beef and break it apart with a wooden spoon. Cook 6-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned.

steps.title: Bloom the spices
steps.text: Add chili powder, cumin, sugar, tomato paste, garlic powder, salt, black pepper, and optional cayenne. Stir until the beef is evenly coated and fragrant.

steps.title: Add the liquids and beans
steps.text: Add beef broth, diced tomatoes with their juice, drained kidney beans, and tomato sauce. Stir well.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Bring to a low boil, then reduce to low or medium-low. Simmer uncovered 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Remove from heat and rest 5-10 minutes. Serve with cheddar, sour cream, green onions, crackers, or avocado.

recipe.note: Chili powder brands vary a lot in heat. Start with a mild brand for a family-friendly pot, then offer hot sauce at the table.

recipe.title: Sam's Fried
recipe.subtitle: Chicken
recipe.description: Buttermilk-marinated chicken with a deeply seasoned, extra-craggy fried crust.

items: ¼ cup hot sauce, such as Tabasco or Cholula
2 tsp each garlic powder, white pepper, Spanish paprika, mustard powder, celery salt, onion powder, MSG, and oregano

steps.title: Slice the chicken
steps.text: Slice each chicken breast lengthwise so the pieces cook evenly and form thinner, crispier cutlets.

steps.title: Make the marinade
steps.text: Whisk buttermilk, kosher salt, garlic powder, white pepper, cayenne, and hot sauce together in a bowl.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Add chicken, cover, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour or overnight for deeper seasoning.

steps.title: Season the dredge
steps.text: Whisk flour, kosher salt, garlic powder, paprika, white pepper, mustard powder, celery salt, black pepper, onion powder, MSG, oregano, and cayenne in a medium bowl.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Add about 2½ inches of oil to a heavy-bottomed pot, leaving plenty of headroom. Heat to 350°F.

steps.title: Dredge thoroughly
steps.text: Press each piece of marinated chicken firmly into the seasoned flour so every surface is coated. Shake off only the loose excess.

steps.title: Fry and rest
steps.text: Fry in batches for 5–7 minutes, turning as needed, until deeply golden and the center reaches 165°F. Transfer to a wire rack so the crust stays crisp.

recipe.note: Keep the oil near 350°F and avoid crowding the pot. Crowding drops the temperature and makes the crust greasy instead of crunchy.

recipe.title: Sammy's
recipe.subtitle: Chuck roast
recipe.description: A seasoned, slow-cooked chuck roast with potatoes, carrots, bell pepper, and homemade gravy.

items: Seasoned salt and black pepper, to taste
1 tsp each garlic powder, onion powder, cumin, and thyme
½ tsp each Cajun seasoning and red chili powder

steps.title: Season and sear
steps.text: Season the chuck roast with seasoned salt, pepper, and minced garlic. Sear in a large skillet over medium-high heat until browned on all sides, about 2–3 minutes per side.

steps.title: Layer the vegetables
steps.text: Place quartered potatoes, halved carrots, and sliced bell pepper in the bottom of a crockpot.

steps.title: Rub with spices
steps.text: Rub the seared roast with garlic powder, onion powder, cumin, thyme, Cajun seasoning, and red chili powder.

steps.title: Build the crockpot
steps.text: Set the roast on top of the vegetables and pour the beef stock over everything.

steps.title: Cook low and slow
steps.text: Cover and cook on low for 8 hours, until the roast is tender and pulls apart easily.

steps.title: Make the gravy
steps.text: Transfer the roast and vegetables to a serving dish. Slowly whisk cornstarch into the crockpot liquid until it thickens into a smooth gravy.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pour the gravy over the roast and vegetables, then serve hot.

recipe.note: Sear the roast before slow cooking. The browned crust adds depth to both the meat and the beef-stock gravy.

recipe.title: Cinnabon Rolls
recipe.subtitle: But better
recipe.description: Pillowy homemade cinnamon rolls with a deeply spiced filling and rich cream-cheese vanilla glaze.

items: 4 cups (580 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for bench flour
¾ tsp (6 g) fine sea salt
⅓ cup (84 g) unsalted butter, softened
⅓ cup (84 g) unsalted butter, softened, plus more for greasing
3 tbsp (45 ml) whole milk, plus more if needed
½ vanilla bean, seeds scraped from pod

steps.title: Mix the dry ingredients
steps.text: In a stand-mixer bowl, whisk flour, sugar, and salt until evenly combined. Add softened butter and work it into the flour with two forks or your fingers.

steps.title: Add yeast and enrichments
steps.text: Warm milk to about 100°F (38°C), then whisk in instant yeast. With the dough hook on medium-low, add the yeast milk, eggs, and egg yolk. Mix 2-3 minutes until smooth and pulled together.

steps.title: Knead and first rise
steps.text: Turn dough onto a lightly floured surface and knead 30-60 seconds until completely smooth. Transfer to a greased bowl, cover, and let rise at room temperature until doubled, about 90 minutes.

steps.title: Make the filling
steps.text: Whisk light brown sugar, muscovado sugar if using, and cinnamon together until evenly combined.

steps.title: Roll and fill
steps.text: Punch down dough and roll it into a 27-inch-long, ¼-inch-thick rectangle, with the long edge facing you. Spread softened butter over the surface, sprinkle on the cinnamon sugar, and lightly pat it in.

steps.title: Shape the rolls
steps.text: Starting at the bottom long edge, tightly roll dough into a log. Use a serrated knife to cut twelve 2-inch-thick rolls.

steps.title: Second rise
steps.text: Grease a 9-by-13-inch baking dish with softened butter. Arrange rolls in four rows of three, turning the tails toward neighboring rolls. Cover and rise until about 1½ times their original size, 30-45 minutes.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Heat oven to 375°F (190°C). Bake 15-20 minutes until golden brown, then cool in the pan for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Glaze and serve
steps.text: Whip cream cheese until smooth. Beat in powdered sugar, then whisk in milk until the glaze falls easily from a spoon. Add more milk one teaspoon at a time if needed, stir in vanilla bean seeds, drizzle over the warm rolls, and serve.

recipe.note: For an extra-rich finish, add a little cinnamon-sugar butter and a splash of heavy cream to the pan before baking, as suggested by one of the recipe's reviewers.

recipe.title: Authentic NY
recipe.subtitle: Style pizza
recipe.description: A thin, foldable New York slice with chewy cold-fermented dough, crisp bottom, browned cheese, and a lightly charred crust.

items: 50 g sifted spelt or rye flour, optional
Vital wheat gluten, optional if using bread flour
Crushed or whole peeled canned tomatoes
Salt and dried oregano, to taste
Semolina or semola flour, for the peel

steps.title: Mix and autolyse
steps.text: Combine flours and water until no dry flour remains. Cover and rest 20 minutes so the flour hydrates and begins developing gluten.

steps.title: Add and knead
steps.text: Add yeast, salt, and sugar. Mix until incorporated, rest another 20 minutes, then knead about 5 minutes until smooth and elastic. If sticky, let it rest 1–2 minutes before continuing.

steps.title: Bulk ferment and divide
steps.text: Form a tight ball and leave covered at room temperature until roughly doubled or tripled, about 1–3 hours. Divide into two equal portions and form tight dough balls.

steps.title: Cold ferment
steps.text: Place dough balls in roomy covered containers and refrigerate 2–3 days. This is the sweet spot for flavor and dough strength.

steps.title: Make uncooked sauce
steps.text: Blend tomatoes with salt and oregano until smooth but still tomato-forward. Add a little sugar only if needed. Do not cook the sauce; dilute only very concentrated tomato products.

steps.title: Heat the steel
steps.text: Position a baking steel on the second-highest rack. Heat the oven as hot as it will go, ideally 550°F / 290°C, for at least 1 hour and preferably 90 minutes. Take dough out while the oven heats.

steps.title: Shape on a floured surface
steps.text: Dust a wooden peel with semolina. Generously flour dough, press from the center outward while leaving a thicker rim, then stretch around the edges with knuckles or fists until it reaches your desired diameter.

steps.title: Top lightly and launch
steps.text: Transfer to the peel. Spiral on a thin, even layer of sauce, add oregano and Pecorino if using, then low-moisture mozzarella. Keep the center light and shake the peel to make sure the pizza slides freely.

steps.title: Bake on steel
steps.text: Bake 4–5 minutes, rotating halfway through, until the crust is browned and lightly charred and the mozzarella is fully melted and just beginning to separate.

steps.title: Cool, then reheat the slice
steps.text: Cool finished pizza on a rack 15–20 minutes, then slice. Return a slice directly to the hot steel under the broiler for 60–90 seconds to crisp the bottom and add more char on top.

recipe.note: A long cold ferment, very hot steel, and the cool-then-reheat slice method are the three keys to a pizzeria-style New York slice at home.

recipe.title: Golden Milk
recipe.subtitle: Banana smoothie
recipe.description: A creamy, warmly spiced turmeric smoothie for one large serving.

items: 1 tsp honey or maple syrup, optional
A few ice cubes if your banana isn’t frozen

steps.title: Add everything
steps.text: Add all ingredients to a blender.

steps.title: Blend until creamy
steps.text: Blend until smooth and creamy, with no banana pieces left behind.

steps.title: Taste and adjust
steps.text: Add a little more honey or maple syrup if you want it sweeter, then blend once more.

recipe.note: The tiny pinch of black pepper pairs well with turmeric, but keep it very small so you don’t taste it. For an extra-creamy smoothie, add 1–2 tablespoons of Greek yogurt or nut butter.

recipe.title: Buckeye
recipe.subtitle: Candy · no wax
recipe.description: Creamy peanut butter centers dipped in chocolate, with no paraffin wax needed.

items: 1 tbsp coconut oil or shortening, optional

steps.title: Make the filling
steps.text: Mix peanut butter, butter, and vanilla until smooth.

steps.title: Add the sugar
steps.text: Stir in powdered sugar a little at a time until the dough is firm enough to roll.

steps.title: Roll and chill
steps.text: Roll into 1-inch balls, place on a parchment-lined tray, and chill for about 30 minutes.

steps.title: Melt the chocolate
steps.text: Melt chocolate chips with coconut oil or shortening, if using, until smooth.

steps.title: Dip each buckeye
steps.text: Stick a toothpick into each peanut butter ball and dip it into chocolate, leaving a small circle of peanut butter showing on top.

steps.title: Set
steps.text: Place back on parchment and let the chocolate set.

recipe.note: Keep them in the fridge so they stay firm. You do not need paraffin wax—the chocolate will set just fine on its own.

recipe.title: Sammy's
recipe.subtitle: Chai latte
recipe.description: A simple, warming stovetop chai with the exact water, milk, and sugar ratio you like.

items: 1 scoop chai mix or 1 chai tea packet

steps.title: Boil the chai
steps.text: Bring ⅔ cup water to a boil with 1 scoop of chai mix or 1 chai tea packet.

steps.title: Sweeten and spice
steps.text: Add 2 scoops of sugar. Add cardamom, clove, and cinnamon if you want extra warm spice.

steps.title: Add the milk
steps.text: Pour in ⅓ cup milk and heat until the chai is hot and steaming.

steps.title: Strain and serve
steps.text: Strain into a cup, then enjoy right away.

recipe.note: For this ratio, use two scoops of sugar for every cup of chai. Adjust the spices to make it as cozy as you like.

recipe.title: Honey Garlic
recipe.subtitle: Glazed salmon
recipe.description: Sticky, sweet, garlicky salmon in one pan and under 20 minutes.

steps.title: Make the glaze
steps.text: Whisk honey, soy sauce, garlic, lemon, and pepper in a small bowl.

steps.title: Sear the salmon
steps.text: Cook salmon in a hot oven-safe skillet, skin-side down if it has skin, until nearly cooked through.

steps.title: Glaze and broil
steps.text: Add butter and glaze, spoon over the fish, then broil briefly until bubbling and lacquered.

steps.title: Serve right away
steps.text: Finish with lemon and serve with rice or greens while the glaze is glossy.

recipe.note: Keep an eye on the broiler—the honey goes from caramelized to burned in a blink.

recipe.title: Garlic Chicken
recipe.subtitle: Gyros with fries
recipe.description: Loaded Greek street-food-style pitas stuffed with garlicky chicken, crisp fries, vegetables, and a bright yogurt sauce.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Mix minced garlic, olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Coat the chicken thoroughly and marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to overnight.

steps.title: Make the garlic sauce
steps.text: Stir Greek yogurt, finely grated garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, and a pinch of salt together. Refrigerate while preparing the rest of the meal.

steps.title: Cook crispy fries
steps.text: Bake, air-fry, or deep-fry the fries until very crisp. Season with salt while hot.

steps.title: Cook and rest the chicken
steps.text: Heat a skillet or grill over medium-high. Cook thighs for 5–7 minutes per side until browned and cooked through. Rest 5 minutes, then slice thinly.

steps.title: Warm the pita
steps.text: Warm each pita briefly in a dry skillet or microwave until soft, flexible, and easy to wrap.

steps.title: Build the gyros
steps.text: Spread garlic sauce down the center of each pita. Add chicken, fries, tomato, red onion, and any lettuce, feta, or parsley you like. Drizzle with more sauce and wrap tightly.

recipe.note: For true loaded-street-food flavor, toss hot fries with oregano, garlic powder, and lemon zest before adding them to the gyro.

recipe.title: Tuna Salad
recipe.subtitle: The savory one
recipe.description: Creamy, savory tuna salad with hard-boiled eggs and just enough Worcestershire to make it special.

items: 1–2 tbsp finely diced onion or green onion

steps.title: Get everything ready
steps.text: Drain the tuna well, chop the eggs, and finely dice the onion or green onion.

steps.title: Mix until creamy
steps.text: Combine tuna, eggs, mayonnaise, Worcestershire, mustard, onion, salt, and pepper in a bowl.

steps.title: Taste and tune
steps.text: Add another small splash of Worcestershire if you want a more savory flavor. Fold in relish, paprika, or lemon if using.

steps.title: Serve your way
steps.text: Pile it on toast, crackers, lettuce wraps, or between two slices of bread.

recipe.note: Start with two tablespoons of mayonnaise, then add the third only if you want it extra creamy.

recipe.title: Gingerbread
recipe.subtitle: Cookies
recipe.description: Soft-centered, crisp-edged gingerbread cookies with lots of molasses and a confident amount of spice.

items: 1 tsp baking soda + ½ tsp salt
½ tsp each allspice and cloves
⅔ cup unsulphured or dark molasses
Cookie icing, royal icing, or buttercream

steps.title: Whisk the dry ingredients
steps.text: Whisk flour, baking soda, salt, ginger, cinnamon, allspice, and cloves together in a medium bowl.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Beat butter until creamy, then beat in brown sugar and molasses. Add egg and vanilla, then mix in the dry ingredients on low until a thick, slightly sticky dough forms.

steps.title: Chill two discs
steps.text: Divide dough in half, wrap each portion, and pat into a disc. Chill for at least 3 hours and up to 3 days.

steps.title: Roll and cut
steps.text: Heat oven to 350°F. Roll one chilled disc to ¼-inch thick on a generously floured surface, cut shapes, and place them 1 inch apart on lined baking sheets.

steps.title: Bake and cool
steps.text: Bake 9–10 minutes (adjust for cutter size). Cool on the sheet for 5 minutes, then move to a rack to cool completely.

steps.title: Decorate
steps.text: Ice only after the cookies are fully cool. Add the smiles, bow-ties, and buttons.

recipe.note: The long chill is what keeps the shapes tidy. If the dough gets sticky while rolling, flour the surface and return it to the fridge for a few minutes.

recipe.title: Chicken
recipe.subtitle: Fried rice
recipe.description: A fast, takeout-style chicken fried rice with toasted cold rice, egg, vegetables, and a savory sesame finish.

items: 1 lb boneless chicken breast or thighs, diced small
1 tbsp oyster sauce, optional but recommended

steps.title: Cook the chicken
steps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add chicken, season lightly with salt and pepper, and cook until browned and cooked through. Transfer to a plate.

steps.title: Scramble the eggs
steps.text: Add a little more oil if needed. Pour in the beaten eggs and scramble until just cooked. Remove them, or push them to one side of the pan.

steps.title: Stir-fry the vegetables
steps.text: Add peas, carrots, garlic, and most of the green onions. Stir-fry for 1–2 minutes until fragrant and hot.

steps.title: Fry the rice
steps.text: Add cold rice and break up every clump. Cook for 3–4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the rice is hot and beginning to toast.

steps.title: Season over high heat
steps.text: Return chicken and eggs to the pan. Add soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sesame oil, then toss over high heat for another 1–2 minutes.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Taste and add more soy sauce, salt, or pepper if needed. Top with the remaining green onions and serve immediately.

recipe.note: Use rice that was cooked and refrigerated beforehand. Cold, slightly dry rice fries beautifully and will not turn mushy.

recipe.title: Chana
recipe.subtitle: Masala
recipe.description: A warm North Indian chickpea curry simmered in a fragrant onion-tomato masala with plenty of spices and herbs.

items: 1 cup dried chickpeas, or 2 cans (15 oz each) chickpeas
1½ cups water for pressure-cooking, plus more for gravy
¾ tsp salt, plus more to taste
1½ tsp Kashmiri red chili powder, adjust to taste
1 tsp kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), optional
¼ tsp amchur (dried mango powder), optional

steps.title: Soak and cook the chickpeas
steps.text: If using dried chickpeas, rinse and soak in 3½–4 cups water overnight or at least 8 hours. Drain, rinse, and pressure-cook with 1½ cups fresh water for 5–6 whistles, or use an Instant Pot on high pressure for 18 minutes. They should mash easily when squeezed. For canned chickpeas, drain and rinse them well.

steps.title: Bloom the whole spices
steps.text: Heat oil in a large pot. If using, add bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, and cardamoms; let them sizzle briefly.

steps.title: Cook the aromatics
steps.text: Add onion and green chili if using. Sauté until light golden, about 8–9 minutes. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute without browning it.

steps.title: Make the tomato masala
steps.text: Add tomatoes and salt. Cook 6–7 minutes until soft, pulpy, and thick. Stir in red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, coriander powder, and cumin powder; sauté 3–4 minutes until fragrant.

steps.title: Blend if you like
steps.text: For a smooth gravy, discard the bay leaf and cinnamon, cool the masala, then blend it with 2 tablespoons cooked chickpeas. Return the puree to the pot. Skip this step for a chunkier curry.

steps.title: Simmer the chana
steps.text: Add chickpeas with about 1¼ cups cooking stock, then add ¾–1 cup more water as needed. For canned chickpeas, add about 1¾ cups water. Taste for salt, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until thick.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Crush kasuri methi between your palms and stir it in with amchur. Garnish with cilantro and lemon juice if desired. Serve with basmati rice, jeera rice, naan, roti, or chapati.

recipe.note: Canned chickpeas should be tender but still hold their shape. The tomato gravy is acidic, so chickpeas will not soften much after they go into the masala.

recipe.title: Chicken
recipe.subtitle: Pakora
recipe.description: Crispy Andhra-style chicken pakora with a lightly spiced gram-flour coating and tender chicken inside.

items: ½ lb boneless chicken, cut into bite-size pieces
¼ cup onion, finely chopped or thinly sliced, optional
¾–1 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder
⅓ tsp salt, plus more to taste
2 sprigs curry leaves, or 2 tbsp chopped mint or cilantro

steps.title: Season the flour
steps.text: Mix besan, rice flour, salt, turmeric, red chili powder, and garam masala in a large bowl. Taste a tiny pinch and adjust salt or spice before adding chicken.

steps.title: Build the coating
steps.text: Add ginger-garlic paste, onion, herbs, green chilies if using, chicken, and egg white. Add only enough water to form a thick, stiff, dough-like coating, not a loose batter.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Heat oil in a deep pan over medium to medium-high heat. A small piece of coating should sizzle and rise slowly without browning immediately.

steps.title: Fry in batches
steps.text: Slide coated chicken pieces gently into the oil without crowding. Leave untouched for 2 minutes, then stir and fry until golden and crisp.

steps.title: Drain and serve
steps.text: Transfer pakora to a wire rack or steel colander. Bring oil back to temperature between batches and serve hot with green chutney or masala chai.

recipe.note: Rice flour or cornstarch is what keeps these crisp. Too much water makes the coating soft, so add it a little at a time.

recipe.title: Chicken
recipe.description: Crispy South Indian chicken with curry leaves, warming spice, and an optional punchy chili-garlic tempering.

items: 1.3 lb boneless chicken, cut into ¾-inch pieces
2 tbsp rice flour or all-purpose flour
4–6 green chilies, slit, seeded, and dried thoroughly

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix chicken with ginger-garlic paste, salt, red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, chopped curry leaves, yogurt, and lemon juice. Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour, or up to 36 hours.

steps.title: Make the coating
steps.text: When ready to fry, add cornstarch, rice flour, and egg white to the chicken. Mix to a moist coating that clings well. Add only a splash of water if it feels too dry.

steps.title: Fry crisp
steps.text: Heat oil over medium. Fry chicken in batches without disturbing it for the first 2 minutes. Stir and fry until crisp and golden, about 4½–5 minutes per batch.

steps.title: Fry the garnish
steps.text: Lower heat and carefully fry the dried curry leaves until crisp, then fry dried, slit green chilies until lightly blistered. Serve this Chennai-style version as is, or continue with tempering.

steps.title: Temper if desired
steps.text: Warm 2 tablespoons oil in a wok. Fry garlic, curry leaves, and green chilies briefly. Lower heat, stir in the chili-garlic paste, water, and salt, then cook to a thick paste. Turn off heat, toss with fried chicken, and finish with black pepper.

recipe.note: For a kid-friendly version, reduce the chili powder and skip the optional tempering. Keep curry leaves and chilies very dry before frying to prevent splatter.

recipe.title: Butter
recipe.subtitle: Chicken
recipe.description: Silky, restaurant-style chicken makhani with yogurt-marinated chicken, tomatoes, cashews, butter, and cream.

items: 1.1 lb boneless chicken, cut into 1-inch pieces
½–¾ tsp Kashmiri red chili powder
600 g fresh tomatoes, or 1 cup passata

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Mix chicken with chili powder, salt, and lemon juice; rest 20 minutes. Add yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, remaining spices, kasuri methi, and oil. Cover and refrigerate at least 30 minutes, or overnight for the best tenderness.

steps.title: Blend the sauce base
steps.text: If using onion, sauté it in a little oil until lightly golden and cool. Blend onion, tomatoes, cashews, and water into a very smooth puree. Soak cashews in hot water first if your blender needs help.

steps.title: Cook the makhani sauce
steps.text: Melt butter and sizzle whole spices if using. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, then briefly cook the ground spices off heat. Stir in tomato-cashew puree and cook partially covered until thick.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add hot water and simmer 10 minutes until glossy and thick, with traces of butter visible. Remove whole spices if you prefer.

steps.title: Roast the chicken
steps.text: Pan-roast marinated chicken in a little butter or ghee over medium heat in batches until just cooked and the marinade dries up. Avoid overcooking.

steps.title: Finish the butter chicken
steps.text: Add chicken to the sauce and simmer 5–7 minutes. Season with salt, sugar, and kasuri methi, then turn off heat and stir in cream. Garnish with cilantro and serve with rice or naan.

recipe.note: Use thick Greek yogurt and sweet, ripe tomatoes. The sauce gets its signature silky richness from cashews plus cream, not from overloading it with spice.

recipe.title: French Onion
recipe.subtitle: Soup
recipe.description: Deeply caramelized onions in a Worcestershire-beef bouillon broth, finished with baguette and melted Baby Swiss.

items: 1 tsp black pepper, plus more to taste
10–12 oz Baby Swiss cheese, sliced or shredded

steps.title: Caramelize the onions
steps.text: Melt butter with olive oil in a large soup pot over medium-low. Add onions and sugar if using. Cook 35–45 minutes, stirring regularly, until very soft and deep golden brown.

steps.title: Add garlic
steps.text: Stir in garlic and cook about 1 minute until fragrant.

steps.title: Build the broth
steps.text: Add water, beef bouillon, Worcestershire, black pepper, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a gentle boil.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Reduce heat and simmer uncovered 25–30 minutes. Remove bay leaf, then taste before adding salt. Add more pepper or Worcestershire if you want a stronger flavor.

steps.title: Toast the bread
steps.text: Slice baguette into ¾- to 1-inch pieces and toast until lightly browned and crisp.

steps.title: Broil and serve
steps.text: Ladle soup into oven-safe bowls. Top with toast, Baby Swiss, and Parmesan if using. Broil 2–4 minutes, watching closely, until cheese is bubbly and lightly browned.

recipe.note: For an extra-rich bouillon broth, stir in one more tablespoon of butter near the end of simmering.

recipe.title: Easy Meat
recipe.subtitle: Sauce
recipe.description: A simple 30-minute meat sauce for pasta, with ground meat, marinara, oregano, fresh basil, and a little chili heat.

items: 1 lb ground beef or Italian sausage
1 jar (24 oz) marinara or pasta sauce
Salt and black pepper, to taste
Cooked spaghetti, rigatoni, or favorite pasta
A splash of pasta water, optional

steps.title: Brown the meat
steps.text: Brown ground beef or Italian sausage in a large skillet over medium heat, breaking it into small pieces.

steps.title: Cook the aromatics
steps.text: Add onion and cook 3–4 minutes. Add garlic and red chili, then cook 30 seconds more.

steps.title: Drain if needed
steps.text: Drain excess grease if the meat released a lot of fat.

steps.title: Simmer the sauce
steps.text: Stir in marinara and oregano. Simmer gently on low for 10–15 minutes, then taste and season with salt and black pepper.

steps.title: Toss and finish
steps.text: Add a splash of pasta water before combining with cooked pasta. Finish with fresh basil and Parmesan if using.

recipe.note: Pasta water helps the sauce cling to noodles and makes the finished dish feel more cohesive.

recipe.title: Classic
recipe.subtitle: Burgers
recipe.description: Juicy, well-seasoned burgers with a crisp seared crust, melted cheese, and all the classic toppings.

items: ½ red or yellow onion, thinly sliced

steps.title: Shape the patties
steps.text: Divide beef into four loose 6-ounce portions. Gently form patties about ¾ inch thick, then press a shallow dimple in the center of each so they stay flat as they cook.

steps.title: Season right before cooking
steps.text: Season both sides generously with salt, pepper, and garlic powder if using. Do not mix seasonings into the beef, which can make the texture dense.

steps.title: Heat the grill or skillet
steps.text: Heat a grill, cast-iron skillet, or griddle over medium-high until very hot. Lightly oil the surface only if needed.

steps.title: Cook the burgers
steps.text: Cook patties 3–4 minutes on the first side without pressing them down. Flip once and cook 3–4 minutes more for medium, adjusting for your preferred doneness.

steps.title: Melt cheese and toast buns
steps.text: Add cheese during the final minute and cover briefly to melt. Butter and toast buns cut-side down until lightly golden.

steps.title: Build and serve
steps.text: Layer sauce, lettuce, burger, tomato, onion, pickles, and the top bun. Serve immediately with fries, chips, or a salad.

recipe.note: The best burger trick is restraint: handle the beef lightly and never press a cooking patty with a spatula, or you lose the juices.

recipe.title: Classic
recipe.subtitle: Hot dogs
recipe.description: Grilled or pan-seared hot dogs with soft toasted buns and a build-your-own topping lineup.

items: ½ cup water, for skillet steaming
Pickled sport peppers or jalapeños, optional

steps.title: Prep the dogs
steps.text: Make a few shallow diagonal cuts across each hot dog. This helps them heat evenly and gives grilled dogs more crisp edges.

steps.title: Grill method
steps.text: Grill over medium heat for 6–8 minutes, turning every minute or two, until hot throughout with browned, lightly blistered edges.

steps.title: Skillet method
steps.text: For stovetop dogs, add hot dogs and ½ cup water to a skillet over medium heat. Cover and steam 3–4 minutes until water evaporates, then roll dogs in the pan until browned.

steps.title: Toast the buns
steps.text: Butter buns if using and toast them cut-side down on the grill or in a skillet until warm and lightly golden.

steps.title: Top your way
steps.text: Place each dog in a bun and add mustard, ketchup, onion, relish, sauerkraut, peppers, cheese, or chili. Serve hot.

recipe.note: Steaming first and browning second gives skillet hot dogs a great snap without drying them out.

recipe.title: Chef Marshall's
recipe.subtitle: Famous challah
recipe.description: A celebratory, honey-kissed braided challah with a glossy egg-washed crust and your choice of cinnamon, sesame, or poppy seeds.

items: 1 egg yolk mixed with water, for egg wash

steps.title: Proof the yeast
steps.text: Mix ½ cup warm water, 1 teaspoon sugar, and active dry yeast. Let stand 2–3 minutes, until foamy.

steps.title: Build the dough
steps.text: In a large mixing bowl, combine the remaining 2 cups warm water, sugar, oil, vanilla, honey, salt, baking powder, yeast mixture, eggs, and 4 cups flour. Begin mixing until combined.

steps.title: Add flour gradually
steps.text: Add most of the remaining flour 2 cups at a time, mixing well after each addition. Reserve 2 cups flour for kneading.

steps.title: Knead and first rise
steps.text: Knead 5 minutes in the mixer, then knead 5 minutes by hand on the table, using reserved flour only as needed. Lightly grease a bowl, cover with a damp cloth, and rest in a warm place until nearly doubled.

steps.title: Second rise
steps.text: Punch down the dough, cover again, and let rise in a warm place until doubled once more.

steps.title: Braid the loaves
steps.text: Punch down dough and divide into three equal portions. For each loaf, make three 10-inch ropes and braid them together.

steps.title: Proof and finish
steps.text: Place braids on greased baking sheets. Brush with egg wash and sprinkle with cinnamon, sesame seeds, or poppy seeds. Cover and rest in a warm spot for 1 hour.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Heat oven to 350°F. Bake 30–40 minutes, until the tops are deeply golden and the loaves sound hollow when tapped.

recipe.note: Use warm, not hot, water for the starter. If it does not foam, the yeast is inactive and the dough will not rise properly.

recipe.title: Goldstein
recipe.subtitle: Snickerdoodles
recipe.description: Soft-centered snickerdoodles with tangy cream of tartar and a generous cinnamon-sugar crackle.

steps.title: Mix the dry ingredients
steps.text: Whisk flour, baking soda, cream of tartar, and salt together in a medium bowl.

steps.title: Cream butter and sugar
steps.text: In a large bowl or stand mixer fitted with the paddle, beat sugar and softened butter on medium speed until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes. Add egg, scrape down the bowl, then mix in vanilla.

steps.title: Finish the dough
steps.text: Set mixer to low and gradually add the dry ingredients. Beat only until just combined, then scrape down the bowl and incorporate any remaining dry bits.

steps.title: Make the coating
steps.text: Stir sugar and cinnamon together in a small bowl until evenly combined.

steps.title: Shape and coat
steps.text: Roll dough into 30 g balls, coat each one in cinnamon sugar, and place 2 inches apart on a baking sheet. Press each ball down slightly.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake at 350°F for 11 minutes. Let cookies cool briefly on the baking sheet before moving them to a rack.

recipe.note: Take the cookies out when the centers still look soft. They will finish setting as they cool, keeping the middle tender.

recipe.title: Joshua Weissman's
recipe.subtitle: Raising Cane's chicken
recipe.description: Sammy's favorite Raising Cane's-style chicken-tender combo: crisp buttermilk chicken, seasoned fries, buttery Texas toast, slaw, and a punchy signature sauce.

items: 4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts, halved lengthwise
2 tsp each garlic powder, paprika, and white pepper
½ head green cabbage, thinly sliced
½ cup mayonnaise + ¼ cup buttermilk

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Stir mayonnaise, ketchup, Worcestershire, garlic, salt, and black pepper together. Refrigerate at least 1 hour so the flavor settles in.

steps.title: Mix the slaw
steps.text: Combine mayo, buttermilk, lemon, grated carrot and pickle, then fold in cabbage. Season to taste and keep chilled.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Whisk buttermilk with salt, garlic powder, and white pepper. Coat the chicken and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, or overnight.

steps.title: Prepare the fries
steps.text: Cut potatoes into thin batons and soak in cold salted water for 30 minutes. Dry thoroughly, fry once at 300°F until softened, then again at 400°F until crisp. Salt immediately.

steps.title: Dredge and fry
steps.text: Mix flour with salt, garlic powder, paprika, and white pepper. Press each tender firmly into the flour, then fry at 350°F in small batches for 5–7 minutes, until deeply golden and cooked through.

steps.title: Make Texas toast and serve
steps.text: Melt butter with garlic, toast bread in the butter on both sides, brush with more garlic butter, and finish with flaky salt. Serve each plate with two tenders, fries, slaw, toast, and the sauce.

recipe.note: Credit: adapted from Joshua Weissman's 'Making Raising Cane's Chicken Finger Combo At Home | But Better' (joshuaweissman.com).

recipe.title: Addison's Fish Sauce
recipe.subtitle: Chicken wings
recipe.description: Crispy air-fried chicken wings with a simple sweet-savory fish-sauce marinade and a fresh green-onion finish.

items: 2 lb chicken wings, split at joints and patted dry
Cooking spray or neutral oil spray

steps.title: Season and marinate
steps.text: Add wings, fish sauce, sugar, garlic powder, and onion powder to a large zip-top bag. Seal, shake until coated, then refrigerate for 2–4 hours.

steps.title: Coat the wings
steps.text: Remove the wings from the bag and coat evenly in cornstarch. Shake away loose excess so the coating stays light and crisp.

steps.title: Air-fry crisp
steps.text: Preheat the air fryer to 400°F. Arrange wings in a single layer, lightly spray with oil, and air-fry for 7 minutes. Flip, then continue in short 3–5 minute intervals until crisp, browned, and the thickest piece reaches 165°F.

steps.title: Garnish and serve
steps.text: Transfer the hot wings to a serving plate and shower with sliced green onion. Add lime if you want a bright finish.

recipe.note: Do not crowd the air-fryer basket. Depending on wing size and the air fryer, a second crisping pass after the initial 7 minutes gives the best result.

recipe.title: Easy Homemade
recipe.subtitle: Horchata
recipe.description: A creamy, cinnamon-kissed rice drink made at home with both evaporated and sweetened condensed milk.

items: ½ can (7 oz) sweetened condensed milk
¼ tsp ground cinnamon, plus more for serving

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Add the rice and cinnamon sticks to a blender. Pour in the hot water, pulse a few times to break up the rice, then cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.

steps.title: Blend smooth
steps.text: Blend the soaked rice mixture for 1–2 minutes, until the rice is very finely ground and the mixture looks milky.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Pour through a fine-mesh strainer lined with cheesecloth or a clean thin kitchen towel into a pitcher. Press gently; do not force gritty rice solids through.

steps.title: Make it creamy
steps.text: Whisk in evaporated milk, sweetened condensed milk, vanilla, ground cinnamon, and salt. Taste and add a splash of water if you want it lighter.

steps.title: Chill and serve
steps.text: Refrigerate until cold. Stir well, pour over ice, and finish each glass with a light dusting of cinnamon.

recipe.note: For the smoothest horchata, give the rice a full overnight soak and strain it twice. It keeps chilled for up to 3 days; stir before pouring.

recipe.title: Vietnamese Butterfly Chicken
recipe.subtitle: with Tangy Nước Chấm
recipe.description: Thin chicken breast wrapped in crisp, golden wonton triangles and served hot with a sweet, salty, sour, vinegar-forward nước chấm.

items: 1 Thai chili, finely sliced, or chili-garlic sauce to taste
2–3 Tbsp very thinly shredded carrot, optional

steps.title: Slice the chicken
steps.text: Slice the chicken into thin pieces roughly 2 1/2–3 inches long, about 1 inch wide, and about 1/4 inch thick. Keeping the chicken thin helps it cook through before the wrapper gets too dark.

steps.title: Marinate for 20–30 minutes
steps.text: Mix 1 Tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1 very finely minced garlic clove, 1/2 tsp black pepper, and 1/2 tsp cornstarch. Add the chicken and toss well. Let it marinate for about 20–30 minutes.

steps.title: Make the sauce: dissolve the sugar
steps.text: While the chicken marinates, mix 1 cup warm water and 1/4 cup sugar until the sugar is completely dissolved.

steps.title: Add the lime and vinegar
steps.text: Stir 1/4 cup fresh lime juice and 1/4 cup unseasoned rice vinegar into the sugar water. This sauce is intentionally a little more vinegar-forward because it works especially well with fried chicken.

steps.title: Add the fish sauce
steps.text: Stir in 1/4 cup fish sauce.

steps.title: Finish and rest the nước chấm
steps.text: Add 2–3 very finely minced garlic cloves, 1 finely sliced Thai chili or chili-garlic sauce to taste, and 2–3 Tbsp very thinly shredded carrot if using. Do not add sesame oil. Let the sauce sit for 15–30 minutes before serving so the garlic and chili have time to flavor it.

steps.title: Wrap into triangles
steps.text: Place a wonton wrapper in front of you like a diamond and put one piece of chicken in the center. Lightly wet the edges with water. Fold the wrapper diagonally over the chicken to make a triangle. Press the edges firmly together and push out as much trapped air as possible. Repeat with the remaining chicken.

steps.title: Heat the canola oil
steps.text: Pour enough canola oil into a pot or deep skillet for the chicken packets to float or be mostly submerged. Heat the oil to about 340–350°F. If you do not have an oil thermometer, drop in a small piece of wonton wrapper: it should immediately begin bubbling steadily without turning dark brown right away.

steps.title: Fry in small batches
steps.text: Fry about 4–5 pieces at a time for approximately 3–4 minutes, turning as needed, until the wrappers are crisp and golden and the chicken reaches 165°F internally. Do not overcrowd the oil.

steps.title: Drain and serve immediately
steps.text: Transfer cooked pieces to a wire rack to drain. Serve hot immediately with plenty of tangy nước chấm.

steps.title: Adjust the sauce to taste
steps.text: The sauce should taste sweet, salty, sour, and noticeably tangy. For more tang, add rice vinegar 1 Tbsp at a time; you can increase it to around 1/3 cup total for an especially sharp sauce. If too sour, add a little more sugar. If too salty or fishy, add a splash of water and a little sugar. If too sweet, add more lime juice or rice vinegar. If too mild, add fish sauce 1 Tbsp at a time.

steps.title: Quick game plan
steps.text: 1. Slice and marinate the chicken for 20–30 minutes. 2. Make the nước chấm and let it sit. 3. Wrap the chicken in wonton wrappers. 4. Heat canola oil to 340–350°F. 5. Fry for about 3–4 minutes until crisp and the chicken reaches 165°F. 6. Drain on a rack. 7. Serve hot with plenty of tangy nước chấm.

recipe.note: User-provided recipe, saved in Sammy’s collection. Do not add sesame oil to the nước chấm. Use unseasoned rice vinegar; start with 1/4 cup and increase to around 1/3 cup total if desired. Keep the chicken about 1/4 inch thick and cook to 165°F internally. Total time is an estimate and varies with slicing, wrapping, and the number of frying batches. Representative fried-wonton photo by Polina Tankilevitch / Pexels: https://www.pexels.com/photo/deep-fried-meat-on-a-white-surface-5848530/

recipe.title: Honey Garlic
recipe.subtitle: Chicken Thighs
recipe.description: Skillet chicken thighs in a sweet, garlicky honey-soy sauce, topped with cilantro and great over rice.
recipe.note: Recipe by Eric VanLandingham, from Allrecipes (https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/282124/honey-garlic-chicken-thighs/). Cook's notes: You can use skin-on, skinless, boneless, or bone-in chicken thighs. If using bone-in thighs, allow about 5 to 10 minutes longer than the original cook time. You can use an entire medium head of garlic, chopped, instead of individual cloves. If serving over rice, plan on about 3 to 4 cups uncooked rice to serve alongside and soak up the extra sauce. Garnish with fresh parsley instead of cilantro if you like.

items: salt and ground black pepper to taste
2 tablespoons olive oil, or as needed
7 cloves garlic, chopped, or to taste
1 pinch onion powder, or to taste
1 pinch garlic powder, or to taste

steps.title: Gather
steps.text: Gather all ingredients.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Season chicken on both sides with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Brown
steps.text: Heat olive oil in a cast iron skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken and brown on one side, 3 to 5 minutes.

steps.title: Add aromatics
steps.text: Flip chicken and add onion and garlic; continue to cook until chicken is mostly (but not fully) cooked and onion and garlic are soft, 5 to 7 minutes more. Remove chicken to a plate.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Add honey, soy sauce, onion powder, and garlic powder to the skillet. Stir and scrape the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon to get garlic and onion to mix with the liquid.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Return chicken to the skillet, cover, and reduce heat to medium. Cook until no longer pink in the center and juices run clear, about 10 more minutes, turning once halfway through. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of a thigh should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Arrange chicken on a serving plate and drizzle liquid from the pan on top. Sprinkle with cilantro to serve. Enjoy!

recipe.title: Dewey’s House Salad
recipe.subtitle: Copycat with Balsamic Vinaigrette
recipe.description: Mixed greens with cranberries, goat cheese, toasted pine nuts, balsamic dressing, and optional chicken.
recipe.total: 1 hour 26 min, including minimum chicken marinade
recipe.note: Source: Alaina Hinkle, Honest Grub, Honest Foodie — https://www.honestgrubhonestfoodie.com/easy-copy-cat-deweys-house-salad/. No contributor changes. Chicken is optional. Total calculated from listed prep, cook, and minimum marinade; longer marinating increases total. The source’s nutrition excludes dressing.

items: 6 tbsp balsamic vinegar, more if needed
2 tsp monk fruit sweetener or cane sugar

steps.title: Blend dressing
steps.text: Blend all vinaigrette ingredients with an immersion blender until creamy. Store in an airtight dressing container.

steps.title: Marinate optional chicken
steps.text: Season both sides. In an 8 × 8-inch dish, coat chicken with 1/2 cup dressing. Cover; refrigerate 1–24 hours.

steps.title: Cook optional chicken
steps.text: Melt butter over medium heat until simmering. Add chicken with its coating; discard remaining marinade. Cover pan with foil; cook 7–8 minutes per side, depending on thickness. Rest on a plate.

steps.title: Toast pine nuts
steps.text: Spread nuts evenly in a skillet over medium heat. Stir frequently until golden, about 5 minutes; avoid burning. Cool in a bowl.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Divide greens, cranberries, and cheese among four bowls. Add nuts and dressing; top with sliced chicken if desired.

recipe.title: Autumn's Vodka
recipe.subtitle: Pasta
recipe.description: Creamy, tomato-forward vodka sauce tossed with penne and Parmesan, adapted to be less spicy and kid-approved.
recipe.note: Vodka is optional, but highly encouraged! Recipe by Barbara Sauermann, from Allrecipes (https://www.allrecipes.com/gigi-hadid-pasta-recipe-11900468). Her version adapts the original Gigi Hadid pasta to be less spicy and more tomato-y; increase the red pepper flakes if you like heat. Garnish with chopped basil if you like. Cook's note: If you like a lot of sauce, use less pasta or double the sauce.

items: 1/2 cup pasta cooking water, or as needed
1/2 onion, diced or 1 large shallot, diced
1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes, or to taste
salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste

steps.title: Cook the pasta
steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add penne and cook according to package instructions until just al dente, about 9 minutes. Scoop out 1/2 cup pasta water and set aside. Drain pasta.

steps.title: Build the base
steps.text: Meanwhile, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat and cook onion until soft and translucent, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Stir in tomato paste and cook, stirring, until tomato paste starts to darken and is well combined with the onion, 2 to 3 minutes.

steps.title: Add cream and vodka
steps.text: Pour in heavy cream and vodka and cook, stirring, for 2 minutes until alcohol evaporates. Stir in red pepper flakes and cook, stirring, until well combined. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Stir in butter until melted. Add drained pasta and 1/4 cup pasta water. Add more pasta water depending on how thick you like the sauce. Stir in freshly grated Parmesan cheese, taste, and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Continue cooking for 1 to 2 minutes over low heat until well combined.

recipe.title: Taylor Swift Chai
recipe.subtitle: Cookies
recipe.description: Soft, spiced sugar cookies rolled in cinnamon sugar and topped with a nutmeg milk glaze.
recipe.note: Adapted from Joy the Baker's Taylor Swift's Chai Sugar Cookies (https://joythebaker.com/2021/11/taylor-swifts-chai-sugar-cookies/). Renamed Taylor Swift Chai Cookies.

items: 1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, at room temperature
1/2 cup vegetable oil (I like canola or sunflower oil)
Pinch of fresh cracked black pepper
2 teaspoons of vanilla extract or the seeds of 1 vanilla bean pod
1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg, plus more for sprinkling the top of the cookies

steps.title: Preheat
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Line baking sheet with parchment paper.

steps.title: Cream butter, oil, sugars and spices
steps.text: Using a mixer fitted with a paddle attachment, beat the butter in a large bowl on medium speed for about 1 minute. Add the vegetable oil. It may not fully incorporate with the butter, but that's ok. Add the granulated sugar, powdered sugar, and all of the spices. Beat to combine.

steps.title: Add egg and vanilla
steps.text: Add the egg and vanilla, beating on medium speed until completely incorporated.

steps.title: Add dry ingredients
steps.text: Stir in the flour, baking soda and salt all at once using a wooden spoon or the mixer set on low.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: The dough will be soft. Refrigerate the dough for 1 hour or freeze for 15 minutes just so it's easier to handle.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: For large cookies, dollop 2 Tablespoons of cookie dough onto the cookie sheet about 2 inches apart. For smaller cookies use 1 Tablespoon for each cookie. Press the dough evenly with your fingers or palm to 1/4-inch thickness. Roll each cookie dough in a small bowl of cinnamon sugar.

steps.title: Bake and cool
steps.text: Bake for 12 to 14 minutes for larger cookies or 8 to 10 minutes for smaller cookies. Let the cookies cool on the baking sheet for at least 10 minutes before transferring to racks to cool completely.

steps.title: Glaze and store
steps.text: In a medium bowl, whisk together the glaze ingredients to thick but spreadable. Spread each cooled cookie with glaze just over the center, leaving the edges of the cookie free of glaze. Sprinkle with a bit of fresh nutmeg if you have it. Store cookies in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 4 days.

recipe.title: Autumn’s Appalachian
recipe.subtitle: Nanner Puddin’
recipe.description: A no-cook banana pudding layering creamy vanilla pudding, sliced bananas, and vanilla wafers in a crowd-size dessert.
recipe.note: Chill at least 1 hour before serving. Top with extra crushed wafers just before serving.

items: 12 small firm but ripe bananas, or more as needed

steps.title: Gather
steps.text: Gather all ingredients.

steps.title: Make the pudding
steps.text: Place milk and pudding mix in a large bowl; beat with a whisk for 2 minutes. Whisk in condensed milk until smooth.

steps.title: Fold in topping
steps.text: Stir in vanilla, then fold in whipped topping.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Just before assembling the pudding, slice the bananas and reserve a few wafers for topping. Arrange a layer of the remaining wafers in the bottom of a large glass serving bowl. Top with a layer of banana slices, then a layer of pudding mixture. Repeat the layers, ending with pudding.

steps.title: Chill and serve
steps.text: For best results, chill pudding in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour before serving. Top with extra crushed wafers just before serving. Enjoy!
